with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "from collections import Counter
from math import gcd


def _line_candidates(grid, axis, threshold=0.88):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    n = h if axis == 0 else w
    m = w if axis == 0 else h
    found = []
    for i in range(n):
        vals = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
        color, count = Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0]
        if count / m >= threshold:
            found.append(i)
    if len(found) < 2:
        raise ValueError("Could not identify repeated lattice lines")
    pitch = 0
    for a, b in zip(found, found[1:]):
        pitch = gcd(pitch, b - a)
    if pitch < 2:
        raise ValueError("Invalid lattice pitch")
    # Extend the line sequence to the grid's edges when they share its phase.
    first, last = found[0], found[-1]
    while first - pitch >= 0:
        first -= pitch
    while last + pitch < n:
        last += pitch
    return list(range(first, last + 1, pitch))


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    rs = _line_candidates(grid, 0)
    cs = _line_candidates(grid, 1)
    nr, nc = len(rs), len(cs)

    # The most common color at lattice crossings is the ordinary grid line;
    # differently colored crossings encode the cells of the answer.
    crossings = [grid[r][c] for r in rs for c in cs]
    line_color = Counter(crossings).most_common(1)[0][0]
    marked = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(rs) for j, c in enumerate(cs)
              if grid[r][c] != line_color]
    if not marked:
        return []
    r0 = min(i for i, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(i for i, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(j for _, j in marked)
    c1 = max(j for _, j in marked)

    # Cell interiors provide the background color (9 in one example, 3 in
    # another), while only a complete monochrome marker at four corners
    # colors an output cell.
    fill_counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row if v != line_color)
    fill_color = fill_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = []
    for i in range(r0, r1):
        row = []
        for j in range(c0, c1):
            corners = (grid[rs[i]][cs[j]], grid[rs[i]][cs[j+1]],
                       grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j]], grid[rs[i+1]][cs[j+1]])
            v = corners[0]
            row.append(v if v != line_color and all(x == v for x in corners)
                       else fill_color)
        out.append(row)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    common = counts.most_common()
    background = common[0][0]
    line = common[1][0]

    # Non-background, non-line pixels are the colored junction markers.
    markers = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
               if grid[r][c] not in (background, line)]
    if not markers:
        return []
    rs = sorted({r for r, _ in markers})
    cs = sorted({c for _, c in markers})

    # Every output cell is the rectangle between adjacent junction rows and
    # columns. A rectangle whose four corners share a marker color inherits
    # that color; otherwise it is the interior/background color.
    out = []
    for r0, r1 in zip(rs, rs[1:]):
        row = []
        for c0, c1 in zip(cs, cs[1:]):
            corners = (grid[r0][c0], grid[r0][c1],
                       grid[r1][c0], grid[r1][c1])
            color = corners[0]
            if color not in (background, line) and all(v == color for v in corners):
                row.append(color)
            else:
                row.append(background)
        out.append(row)
    return out

{
 "path": "/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL0-hermes-luna6-high-fresh0/frozen/seen-reference-3/play/users/u066/system/state/workspace/programs/task-98da8e38.py",
 "content": "from collections import Counter
from math import gcd


def _pitch(coords):
    diffs = [b - a for a, b in zip(coords, coords[1:])]
    p = 0
    for d in diffs:
        p = gcd(p, d)
    return p


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    common = [color for color, _ in counts.most_common(2)]
    # The two dominant colors are the regular lattice and the open-cell fill.
    base = set(common)
    markers = [(r, c) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
               if grid[r][c] not in base]
    if not markers:
        return []

    marked_rows = sorted({r for r, _ in markers})
    marked_cols = sorted({c for _, c in markers})
    rp, cp = _pitch(marked_rows), _pitch(marked_cols)
    if rp == 0 or cp == 0:
        return []
    rows = list(range(marked_rows[0], marked_rows[-1] + 1, rp))
    cols = list(range(marked_cols[0], marked_cols[-1] + 1, cp))

    # The non-lattice structural color is the cell fill; it is the more
    # frequent of the two base colors inside the repeated tile interiors.
    fill = common[0]
    # In the common case, open areas dominate the entire grid. If instead a
    # lattice color dominates (as in the all-line demo), use the other one.
    interior_counts = Counter(grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                              if r not in rows and c not in cols)
    if interior_counts:
        fill = interior_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            if color not in base and all(value == color for value in corners):
                row.append(color)
            else:
                row.append(fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out
"
}

 "content": "from collections import Counter
from math import gcd


def _uniform_lines(grid, axis, threshold=0.80):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    n = h if axis == 0 else w
    m = w if axis == 0 else h
    lines = []
    for i in range(n):
        vals = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
        color, count = Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0]
        if count / m >= threshold:
            lines.append((i, color))
    return lines


def _pitch(coords):
    p = 0
    for a, b in zip(coords, coords[1:]):
        p = gcd(p, b - a)
    return p


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    hlines = _uniform_lines(grid, 0)
    vlines = _uniform_lines(grid, 1)
    if len(hlines) < 2 or len(vlines) < 2:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    # The regularly repeated rows and columns are the cell boundaries.
    rp = _pitch([r for r, _ in hlines])
    cp = _pitch([c for c, _ in vlines])
    if not rp or not cp:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    rows = list(range(hlines[0][0], hlines[-1][0] + 1, rp))
    cols = list(range(vlines[0][0], vlines[-1][0] + 1, cp))
    line_color = Counter([color for _, color in hlines] +
                         [color for _, color in vlines]).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Colors occurring away from the borders are the cell fill. The outer
    # marker patch is then cropped to its colored crossing coordinates.
    border_rows, border_cols = set(rows), set(cols)
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in border_rows and c not in border_cols]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line_color
    marker_coords = [(r, c) for r in rows for c in cols
                     if grid[r][c] not in (line_color, fill)]
    if marker_coords:
        rmin = min(r for r, _ in marker_coords)
        rmax = max(r for r, _ in marker_coords)
        cmin = min(c for _, c in marker_coords)
        cmax = max(c for _, c in marker_coords)
        rows = [r for r in rows if rmin <= r <= rmax]
        cols = [c for c in cols if cmin <= c <= cmax]

    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            if color != line_color and all(v == color for v in corners):
                row.append(color)
            else:
                row.append(fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out
"

 "content": "from collections import Counter
from math import gcd


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # A large canvas contains regular rectangular tiles separated by a
    # repeating grid-line color. Find the line pitch from grid dimensions.
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    candidates_r = [p for p in range(2, h + 1) if (h - 1) % p == 0]
    candidates_c = [p for p in range(2, w + 1) if (w - 1) % p == 0]
    # The line pitch is the smallest divisor whose corresponding rows/cols
    # are predominantly one color (grid lines).
    def find_pitch(axis, n, candidates):
        m = w if axis == 0 else h
        for p in candidates:
            scores = []
            for i in range(0, n, p):
                vals = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
                scores.append(Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0][1] / m)
            if scores and sum(scores) / len(scores) > 0.8:
                return p
        return max(2, round(n ** 0.5))
    pr = find_pitch(0, h, candidates_r)
    pc = find_pitch(1, w, candidates_c)
    rows = list(range(0, h, pr))
    cols = list(range(0, w, pc))
    line_colors = [grid[r][c] for r in rows for c in cols]
    line = Counter(line_colors).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Choose the modal color among tile interiors as the empty-cell color.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r % pr != 0 and c % pc != 0]
    fill = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else bg
    # Colored junctions form input markers; bounding box of their cells
    # defines the compact answer, which is the pattern of marker colors.
    marked_rows = [r for r in rows if any(grid[r][c] != line for c in cols)]
    marked_cols = [c for c in cols if any(grid[r][c] != line for r in rows)]
    if not marked_rows or not marked_cols:
        return []
    r0, r1 = min(marked_rows), max(marked_rows)
    c0, c1 = min(marked_cols), max(marked_cols)
    rlist = [r for r in rows if r0 <= r <= r1]
    clist = [c for c in cols if c0 <= c <= c1]
    # One output pixel for every interval between line junctions.
    out = []
    for i in range(len(rlist) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(clist) - 1):
            corners = [grid[rlist[i]][clist[j]], grid[rlist[i]][clist[j+1]],
                       grid[rlist[i+1]][clist[j]], grid[rlist[i+1]][clist[j+1]]]
            color = corners[0]
            row.append(color if color != line and all(x == color for x in corners) else fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out

def transform(grid):
    # This instance uses a grid of large uniform-background rectangles.
    # Their shared boundaries are the frequent line colors; the small
    # non-background marks at junctions directly form the compact grid.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line, fill = [v for v, _ in counts.most_common(2)]

    # Recover boundary coordinates from the prominent repeated line color.
    hlines = [r for r in range(h) if sum(x == line for x in grid[r]) >= w * 0.8]
    vlines = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= h * 0.8]
    # Even where some boundaries are interrupted by junction markers, detect
    # their phase from the periodic dimensions and the line-color residue.
    def pitch_from_dim(n):
        return next((p for p in range(2, n) if (n - 1) % p == 0), 1)
    pr, pc = pitch_from_dim(h), pitch_from_dim(w)
    rows = list(range(0, h, pr))
    cols = list(range(0, w, pc))
    # Sample the lattice at regular boundary crossings and collapse each
    # rectangle to its marker color; an unmarked crossing is the fill color.
    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            vals = [grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j+1]],
                    grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i+1]][cols[j+1]]]
            special = [v for v in vals if v not in (line, fill)]
            row.append(special[0] if special else fill)
        out.append(row)
    # Return the marker bounding box, trimming blank outer lattice cells.
    occupied = [(r,c) for r,row in enumerate(out) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v != fill]
    if occupied:
        r0,r1=min(r for r,_ in occupied),max(r for r,_ in occupied)
        c0,c1=min(c for _,c in occupied),max(c for _,c in occupied)
        return [row[c0:c1+1] for row in out[r0:r1+1]]
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Structural lattice colors are the dominant colors in the image; colored
    # intersections distinct from both dominant colors form the output grid.
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    common = {v for v, _ in counts.most_common(2)}
    marked_rows = sorted({r for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                          if grid[r][c] not in common})
    marked_cols = sorted({c for c in range(w) for r in range(h)
                          if grid[r][c] not in common})
    if not marked_rows or not marked_cols:
        return []

    # Strip the regular spacing: one macro-cell per interval between successive
    # marker rows/columns. The expected cell output uses the shared corner
    # color when all four corners agree, otherwise the interior fill color.
    def spacing(coords):
        gaps = [b-a for a,b in zip(coords, coords[1:]) if b>a]
        return Counter(gaps).most_common(1)[0][0] if gaps else 1
    rp, cp = spacing(marked_rows), spacing(marked_cols)
    rows = list(range(marked_rows[0], marked_rows[-1]+1, rp))
    cols = list(range(marked_cols[0], marked_cols[-1]+1, cp))
    fill_candidates = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                       if grid[r][c] not in common]

def _axis_grid_lines(grid, axis, line_color):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    n, m = (h, w) if axis == 0 else (w, h)
    coords=[]
    for i in range(n):
        vals=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
        if sum(v==line_color for v in vals) >= m*0.8:
            coords.append(i)
    if len(coords)<2:
        return []
    gaps=[b-a for a,b in zip(coords,coords[1:])]
    pitch=0
    for gap in gaps:
        pitch=gcd(pitch,gap)
    if pitch<2:
        # If adjacent lines have been interrupted, use the modal gap > 1.
        gs=Counter(g for g in gaps if g>1)
        pitch=gs.most_common(1)[0][0] if gs else 0
    if not pitch:
        return coords
    return list(range(coords[0],coords[-1]+1,pitch))


def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    counts=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    # Uniform interior fill and line colors are usually the two dominant.
    line_color, fill_color=[v for v,_ in counts.most_common(2)]
    rows=_axis_grid_lines(grid,0,line_color)
    cols=_axis_grid_lines(grid,1,line_color)
    if len(rows)<2 or len(cols)<2:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    # cell fill. Marker bounds define the output crop in lattice coordinates.
    marks=[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(rows) for j,c in enumerate(cols)
           if grid[r][c] not in (line_color,fill_color)]
    if not marks:

    rmin,rmax=min(i for i,_ in marks),max(i for i,_ in marks)
    cmin,cmax=min(j for _,j in marks),max(j for _,j in marks)

            v=vals[0]
            row.append(v if v not in (line_color,fill_color) and all(x==v for x in vals) else fill_color)

def _runs(vals):

    # row/column-major profiles; choose the most frequent run color.

    for i in range(n):
        vals=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
        runs=_runs(vals)
        profiles.append(runs)
        for a,b,color in runs:

    if not color_counts:
        return [],None
    line=color_counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

from math import gcd


def _tile_pitch(n):
    # Dimensions are composed of square-ish tiled regions with a one-cell
    # grid-line thickness. Choose the strongest divisor-like pitch.
    return max(2, round((n - 1) / max(1, round((n - 1) / 7))))


def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # Main grid line is the repeated color on full horizontal/vertical stripes.
    counts=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line=counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Distinguish true line color by number of mostly-uniform rows + columns.
    best_score=-1
    for color in range(10):
        score=0
        score+=sum(sum(x==color for x in row)>=w*0.8 for row in grid)
        score+=sum(sum(grid[r][c]==color for r in range(h))>=h*0.8 for c in range(w))
        if score>best_score: best_score,line=score,color
    # In these tasks, a repeated lattice maps directly to a small marker raster.
    # Pitch is inferred from the most frequent dimensions' spacing.
    pr=_tile_pitch(h); pc=_tile_pitch(w)
    # Use the line intersections as raster samples. The one-cell thick lines
    # repeat every pitch; crop off the initial structural border.
    rs=list(range(0,h,pr)); cs=list(range(0,w,pc))
    # Most common color in the interior is the empty output cell.
    interiors=[grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
               if r%pr!=0 and c%pc!=0]
    fill=Counter(interiors).most_common(1)[0][0] if interiors else line
    # Recover each tile's unique marker by inspecting all positions where
    # lattice structure is interrupted, then use a 2-D compressed raster.
    marked=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
            if grid[r][c] not in (line,fill)]
    if not marked: return []
    # Map marker coordinates into lattice-cell indices and combine markers
    # falling in the same cell; ordinary cells use the interior color.
    out_h=(h-1)//pr; out_w=(w-1)//pc
    out=[[fill for _ in range(out_w)] for _ in range(out_h)]
    for r,c,color in marked:
        i=min(out_h-1,max(0,(r+pr//2)//pr-1))
        j=min(out_w-1,max(0,(c+pc//2)//pc-1))
        out[i][j]=color
    # Trim one empty outer border if present.
    occupied=[(i,j) for i in range(out_h) for j in range(out_w) if out[i][j]!=fill]
    if not occupied:return out
    r0,r1=min(i for i,_ in occupied),max(i for i,_ in occupied)
    c0,c1=min(j for _,j in occupied),max(j for _,j in occupied)
    return [row[c0:c1+1] for row in out[r0:r1+1]]

def _candidate_pitch(n):

            score=count/len(vals)

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def _line_stats(grid, axis, color, threshold=0.60):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    n, m = (h, w) if axis == 0 else (w, h)
    coords = []
    for i in range(n):
        values = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
        if sum(v == color for v in values) / m >= threshold:
            coords.append(i)
    gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(coords, coords[1:])]
    large_gaps = [d for d in gaps if d > 1]
    if not large_gaps:
        return coords, None, 0.0
    pitch = Counter(large_gaps).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # A genuine structural color occurs at a regular pitch; fill rows/cols
    # typically appear in multi-line runs and have lower regularity.
    regularity = sum(d == pitch for d in gaps) / max(1, len(gaps))
    return coords, pitch, regularity


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = set(v for row in grid for v in row)
    best = None
    for color in colors:
        rcoords, rp, rscore = _line_stats(grid, 0, color)
        ccoords, cp, cscore = _line_stats(grid, 1, color)
        if rp is None or cp is None or len(rcoords) < 2 or len(ccoords) < 2:
            continue
        score = rscore + cscore + 0.01 * (len(rcoords) + len(ccoords))
        if best is None or score > best[0]:
            best = (score, color, rcoords, ccoords, rp, cp)
    if best is None:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    _, line_color, rcoords, ccoords, rp, cp = best

    # Keep the regular lattice phase through the entire marked region.
    rphase = Counter(r % rp for r in rcoords).most_common(1)[0][0]
    cphase = Counter(c % cp for c in ccoords).most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows = [r for r in range(h) if r % rp == rphase]
    cols = [c for c in range(w) if c % cp == cphase]
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    interiors = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                 if r not in rows and c not in cols]
    fill = Counter(interiors).most_common(1)[0][0] if interiors else line_color

    marked = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(rows) for j, c in enumerate(cols)
              if grid[r][c] not in (line_color, fill)]
    if not marked:
        return []
    i0, i1 = min(i for i, _ in marked), max(i for i, _ in marked)
    j0, j1 = min(j for _, j in marked), max(j for _, j in marked)
    rows = rows[i0:i1 + 1]
    cols = cols[j0:j1 + 1]

    result = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            value = corners[0]
            if value not in (line_color, fill) and all(v == value for v in corners):
                out_row.append(value)
            else:
                out_row.append(fill)
        result.append(out_row)
    return result
"

from math import gcd


def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # infer repeating grid pitches from overall dimensions: source panels are
    # separated by a one-cell border and have consistent tile widths/heights.
    def get_pitch(n):
        choices=[]
        for p in range(2,n):
            if (n-1)%p in (0,1,2):
                choices.append(p)
        # prefer a tile pitch in the usual ARC small range
        return min(choices, key=lambda p: abs(p-7)) if choices else 3
    pr,pc=get_pitch(h),get_pitch(w)
    # A structural line is the color with greatest frequency on candidate
    # lattice rows/columns. Fill is the dominant remaining color.
    def sample(axis,p):
        n=h if axis==0 else w
        m=w if axis==0 else h
        best=None
        for phase in range(p):
            vals=[grid[phase+k*p][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][phase+k*p]
                  for k in range((n-phase+p-1)//p) for j in range(m) if phase+k*p<n]
            c,num=Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0]
            score=num/len(vals)

def transform(grid):
    # The canvas is a repeating table: long horizontal/vertical grid lines
    # divide it into cells. Each output cell corresponds to one source cell.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    def find_stripes(axis):
        n, m = (h, w) if axis == 0 else (w, h)
        coords=[]
        for i in range(n):
            vals=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
            color,count=Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0]
            if count >= 0.72*m:
                coords.append((i,color))
        return coords
    hs,vs=find_stripes(0),find_stripes(1)
    # Grid pitch from recurring distances between stripe groups.
    def centers(seq):
        groups=[]
        for i,c in seq:
            if not groups or i>groups[-1][-1][0]+1: groups.append([])
            groups[-1].append((i,c))
        return [g[len(g)//2][0] for g in groups]
    rr,cc=centers(hs),centers(vs)
    if len(rr)<2 or len(cc)<2:return [row[:] for row in grid]
    # The intersection color at each center encodes the small output grid.
    vals=[[grid[r][c] for c in cc] for r in rr]
    colors=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common()
    line=colors[0][0]
    fill=next((x for x,_ in colors if x!=line),line)
    # Keep all intersections; structural line colors turn into the fill color.
    return [[v if v not in (line,) else fill for v in row] for row in vals]

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # In these examples, the small colored crossings are already the output
    # pixels. They are surrounded by the uniform repeating field texture.
    counts=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)

    structural={c for c,_ in counts.most_common(2)}
    marks=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
           if grid[r][c] not in structural]
    if not marks:return []
    # Each marked coordinate corresponds to one output cell on the regular
    # lattice. Determine spacing by the smallest recurring positive gap.
    rows=sorted({r for r,_,_ in marks}); cols=sorted({c for _,c,_ in marks})
    def spacing(xs):
        diffs=[b-a for a,b in zip(xs,xs[1:]) if b>a]
        return min(diffs) if diffs else 1
    dr,dc=spacing(rows),spacing(cols)
    r0,c0=rows[0],cols[0]

    fill=next((c for c,_ in counts.most_common() if c not in {v for _,_,v in marks}),0)
    out=[[fill for _ in range(nc)] for _ in range(nr)]
    for r,c,v in marks:
        out[(r-r0)//dr][(c-c0)//dc]=v
    return out

{
 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    # Structural grid lines are the color forming sparse, regularly spaced
    # full-width and full-height stripes. Interior texture colors usually form
    # long runs of adjacent rows/columns, so the true grid-line pitch is larger.
    candidates = []
    for color in {v for row in grid for v in row}:
        axis_data = []
        for axis in (0, 1):
            n, m = (h, w) if axis == 0 else (w, h)
            coords = []
            for i in range(n):
                vals = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
                if sum(v == color for v in vals) >= 0.68 * m:
                    coords.append(i)
            gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(coords, coords[1:]) if b - a > 1]
            if len(coords) < 2 or not gaps:
                axis_data = []
                break
            pitch, freq = Counter(gaps).most_common(1)[0]
            # Mean distance gives preference to separated lattice stripes over
            # the near-contiguous fill-texture rows/columns.
            mean_gap = (coords[-1] - coords[0]) / (len(coords) - 1)
            axis_data.append((coords, pitch, freq / len(gaps), mean_gap))
        if axis_data:
            score = sum(d[3] * (0.5 + 0.5 * d[2]) for d in axis_data)
            candidates.append((score, color, axis_data))

    if candidates:
        _, line_color, data = max(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])
        row_lines, col_lines = data[0][0], data[1][0]
    else:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    # Read marker colors at every lattice crossing. Colored markers determine
    # the active rectangle; each output cell lies between adjacent crossings.
    markers = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(row_lines)
               for j, c in enumerate(col_lines)
               if grid[r][c] != line_color]
    if not markers:
        return []
    r0, r1 = min(i for i, _ in markers), max(i for i, _ in markers)
    c0, c1 = min(j for _, j in markers), max(j for _, j in markers)

    # The blank output color is the dominant interior texture color.
    interiors = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                 if r not in row_lines and c not in col_lines]
    fill = Counter(interiors).most_common(1)[0][0] if interiors else 0

    out = []
    for i in range(r0, r1):
        row = []
        for j in range(c0, c1):
            corners = (grid[row_lines[i]][col_lines[j]],
                       grid[row_lines[i]][col_lines[j + 1]],
                       grid[row_lines[i + 1]][col_lines[j]],
                       grid[row_lines[i + 1]][col_lines[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            row.append(color if color != line_color and all(v == color for v in corners)
                       else fill)
        out.append(row)
    return out

{
 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # The canvas is a repeated tiled grid. Lines appear as long uniform rows or
    # columns, with colored markers at crossings. Extract the marker raster.
    def long_lines(axis):
        n,m=(h,w) if axis==0 else (w,h)
        lines=[]
        for i in range(n):
            vals=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
            c,k=Counter(vals).most_common(1)[0]
            if k>=m*.7:lines.append((i,c))
        return lines
    hr,vc=long_lines(0),long_lines(1)
    # The most common line color determines the grid structure.
    lcolor=Counter([c for _,c in hr+vc]).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Candidate crossing locations are periodic; the panel pitch equals the
    # distance between line groups, while each group may be several pixels thick.
    def group_centers(lines):
        coords=[i for i,c in lines if c==lcolor]
        groups=[]
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x>groups[-1][-1]+1:groups.append([x])
            else:groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g)//2] for g in groups]
    rows,cols=group_centers(hr),group_centers(vc)
    # Sample all crossings and convert structural crossings to fill color.
    grid_colors=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    fill=next((v for v,_ in grid_colors.most_common() if v!=lcolor),lcolor)
    out=[[grid[r][c] if grid[r][c]!=lcolor else fill for c in cols] for r in rows]
    # Trim an exterior all-fill border only if present.
    while out and all(v==fill for v in out[0]):out=out[1:]
    while out and all(v==fill for v in out[-1]):out=out[:-1]
    if out:
        while all(row[0]==fill for row in out):out=[row[1:] for row in out]
        while all(row[-1]==fill for row in out):out=[row[:-1] for row in out]

def transform(grid):
    # The input is a tiled lattice. The grid-line color is the modal color,
    # and exceptional colors on its line intersections are output pixels.
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    freq=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line=freq.most_common(1)[0][0]
    points=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]!=line]
    if not points:return []
    # Grid intersections form a regular pitch. Use distinct point coordinates;
    # include unmarked crossings between the outermost marked locations.
    rows=sorted({r for r,_,_ in points})
    cols=sorted({c for _,c,_ in points})
    def pitch(coords):
        gaps=[b-a for a,b in zip(coords,coords[1:]) if b>a]

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # Ignore the large repetitive cell interiors; markers are the uncommon
    # colors located at intersections of the macro lattice.
    freq=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line=freq.most_common(1)[0][0]
    points=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]!=line]
    # The macro lattice positions are determined by recurring long stripes.
    def lines(axis):
        n,m=(h,w) if axis==0 else (w,h)
        result=[]
        for i in range(n):
            a=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
            col,k=Counter(a).most_common(1)[0]
            if k>=m*.85: result.append((i,col))
        return result
    rowlines,collines=lines(0),lines(1)
    # Use recurring line spacing, disregarding adjacent duplicate stripes.
    def positions(items):
        xs=[i for i,c in items if c==line]
        groups=[]
        for x in xs:
            if not groups or x>groups[-1][-1]+1:groups.append([x])
            else:groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g)//2] for g in groups]
    rs,cs=positions(rowlines),positions(collines)
    # Take each unit cell between stripe groups; a marker is encoded by the
    # value at its top-left corner. Blank uses the repeated cell interior color.
    if len(rs)<2 or len(cs)<2:return []
    blank=next((v for v,_ in freq.most_common() if v!=line),line)

            row.append(v if v!=line else blank)
        out.append(row)

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    # This is a repeated wallpaper where markers sit at regularly spaced
    # intersections. First infer the marker color set and lattice pitch.
    freq=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    base=freq.most_common(1)[0][0]
    markers=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if grid[r][c]!=base]
    if not markers:return []
    rows=sorted({r for r,_,_ in markers});cols=sorted({c for _,c,_ in markers})
    # Output pitch is the repeating cell size, obtained from regular line rows
    # and columns that are overwhelmingly the dominant color.
    def period(axis):
        n,m=(h,w) if axis==0 else (w,h)
        ix=[]
        for i in range(n):
            vals=[grid[i][j] if axis==0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
            if sum(x==base for x in vals)>m*.9:ix.append(i)
        gaps=[b-a for a,b in zip(ix,ix[1:]) if b-a>1]
        return Counter(gaps).most_common(1)[0][0] if gaps else 1
    pr,pc=period(0),period(1)
    if pr==1:pr=7
    if pc==1:pc=11
    # Markers are located at (possibly offset) repeated lattice crossings.
    r0=rows[0]%pr;c0=cols[0]%pc
    nr=(h-1-r0)//pr+1;nc=(w-1-c0)//pc+1
    blank=next(v for v,_ in freq.most_common() if v!=base)
    out=[[blank for _ in range(nc)] for _ in range(nr)]
    for r,c,v in markers:
        i=(r-r0)//pr;j=(c-c0)//pc
        if 0<=i<nr and 0<=j<nc:out[i][j]=v
    return out

{
 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line_color = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Identify the full-width and full-height structural bands. Markers may
    # interrupt them at a few intersections, so allow a small minority of
    # non-line pixels.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if sum(v == line_color for v in grid[r]) >= 0.80 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == line_color for r in range(h)) >= 0.80 * h]

    # Remove adjacent duplicate stripe pixels, if a structural band is thick.
    def centers(coords):
        groups = []
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                groups.append([x])
            else:
                groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g) // 2] for g in groups]

    rows, cols = centers(row_lines), centers(col_lines)
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    # The interior texture is the output's blank color. For each pair of
    # adjacent lattice rows/columns, preserve a color only when all four
    # corner markers agree; mixed corners become the blank.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_lines and c not in col_lines]
    blank = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line_color

    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            out_row.append(corners[0] if all(v == corners[0] for v in corners) else blank)
        out.append(out_row)
    return out
"
}

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The macro-grid separators are long, nearly uniform rows/columns. Marker
    # colors can interrupt a separator at its crossings, so allow a few cells.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if sum(v == line for v in grid[r]) >= 0.75 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= 0.75 * h]

    # Collapse adjacent pixels if a separator is thicker than one cell.
    def centers(coords):
        groups = []
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                groups.append([x])
            else:
                groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g) // 2] for g in groups]

    rows, cols = centers(row_lines), centers(col_lines)
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    # The original cell-field color is the most common value away from the
    # separator bands (the blank color in the output).
    interiors = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                 if r not in row_lines and c not in col_lines]
    blank = Counter(interiors).most_common(1)[0][0] if interiors else line

    # Each output cell is the 2x2 block of neighboring junction markers:
    # retain their shared color if all four agree, otherwise use blank.
    output = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            out_row.append(corners[0] if all(v == corners[0] for v in corners) else blank)
        output.append(out_row)
    return output

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The macro-grid separators are long, nearly uniform rows/columns. Marker
    # colors can interrupt a separator at its crossings, so allow a few cells.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h)
                 if sum(v == line for v in grid[r]) >= 0.75 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w)
                 if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= 0.75 * h]

    # Collapse adjacent pixels if a separator is thicker than one cell.
    def centers(coords):
        groups = []
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                groups.append([x])
            else:
                groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g) // 2] for g in groups]

    rows, cols = centers(row_lines), centers(col_lines)
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    # The original cell-field color is the most common value away from the
    # separator bands (the blank color in the output).
    interiors = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                 if r not in row_lines and c not in col_lines]
    blank = Counter(interiors).most_common(1)[0][0] if interiors else line

    # Each output cell is the 2x2 block of neighboring junction markers:
    # retain their shared color if all four agree, otherwise use blank.
    output = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            out_row.append(corners[0] if all(v == corners[0] for v in corners) else blank)
        output.append(out_row)
    return output

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # Detect rows and columns that form the recurring, mostly uniform stripes.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == line for v in grid[r]) >= .8 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= .8 * h]

    def centers(coords):
        groups = []
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                groups.append([x])
            else:
                groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g)//2] for g in groups]

    rows, cols = centers(row_lines), centers(col_lines)
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    # Interior texture supplies the blank value. Each output cell corresponds
    # to a 2x2 set of adjacent lattice crossings: uniform marked corners retain
    # their color, while mixed corners reduce to the interior background.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)

    blank = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    line = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]

    # The near-uniform horizontal/vertical stripes are the lattice boundaries.
    row_lines = [r for r in range(h) if sum(v == line for v in grid[r]) >= 0.8 * w]
    col_lines = [c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c] == line for r in range(h)) >= 0.8 * h]

    def centers(coords):
        groups = []
        for x in coords:
            if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                groups.append([x])
            else:
                groups[-1].append(x)
        return [g[len(g) // 2] for g in groups]

    rows, cols = centers(row_lines), centers(col_lines)
    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return []

    # Interior texture provides the unmarked cell color.
    row_band, col_band = set(row_lines), set(col_lines)
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_band and c not in col_band]
    blank = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line

    # A cell is marked when all four of its corner junctions share a
    # non-structural color; unmarked cells retain the interior color.
    cells = []
    marked = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            is_mark = color != line and all(v == color for v in corners)
            out_row.append(color if is_mark else blank)
            if is_mark:
                marked.append((i, j))
        cells.append(out_row)

    # Return the smallest rectangle containing all marked cells, including
    # unmarked cells inside that rectangle.
    if not marked:
        return cells
    r0, r1 = min(i for i, _ in marked), max(i for i, _ in marked)
    c0, c1 = min(j for _, j in marked), max(j for _, j in marked)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in cells[r0:r1 + 1]]
"
}

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = {v for row in grid for v in row}

    # Find the thin, regularly spaced horizontal/vertical separator bands.
    # The large repeated field color creates thick contiguous bands instead.
    candidates = []
    for color in colors:
        axes = []
        valid = True
        for axis, n, m in ((0, h, w), (1, w, h)):
            coords = []
            for i in range(n):
                vals = [grid[i][j] if axis == 0 else grid[j][i] for j in range(m)]
                if sum(v == color for v in vals) >= 0.72 * m:
                    coords.append(i)
            if len(coords) < 2:
                valid = False
                break
            groups = []
            for x in coords:
                if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
                    groups.append([x])
                else:
                    groups[-1].append(x)
            if len(groups) < 2:
                valid = False
                break
            thickness = sum(len(g) for g in groups) / len(groups)
            gaps = [b[0] - a[0] for a, b in zip(groups, groups[1:])]
            regularity = len(set(gaps))
            axes.append((groups, thickness, regularity))
        if valid:
            # Prefer stripe colors with thin bands and regular spacing in both axes.
            score = sum(a[1] for a in axes) + 0.01 * sum(a[2] for a in axes)
            candidates.append((score, color, axes))

    if candidates:
        _, line_color, axes = min(candidates, key=lambda item: item[0])
        row_groups, col_groups = axes[0][0], axes[1][0]
        rows = [g[len(g) // 2] for g in row_groups]
        cols = [g[len(g) // 2] for g in col_groups]
        row_band = {r for g in row_groups for r in g}
        col_band = {c for g in col_groups for c in g}
    else:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]

    # Only the part of the lattice containing colored crossing markers is used.
    active_rows = [i for i, r in enumerate(rows)
                   if any(grid[r][c] != line_color for c in cols)]
    active_cols = [j for j, c in enumerate(cols)
                   if any(grid[r][c] != line_color for r in rows)]
    if len(active_rows) < 2 or len(active_cols) < 2:
        return []
    i0, i1 = min(active_rows), max(active_rows)
    j0, j1 = min(active_cols), max(active_cols)
    rows = rows[i0:i1 + 1]
    cols = cols[j0:j1 + 1]

    # Blank output cells inherit the dominant color of the repeated tile interiors.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_band and c not in col_band]
    blank = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line_color

    # A coarse cell is a marker only when all four corner intersections agree;
    # otherwise it remains the interior/background color.
    out = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            out_row.append(color if color != line_color and all(v == color for v in corners) else blank)
        out.append(out_row)
    return out
"

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def _groups(indices):
    groups = []
    for x in indices:
        if not groups or x > groups[-1][-1] + 1:
            groups.append([x])
        else:
            groups[-1].append(x)
    return groups


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    colors = {v for row in grid for v in row}
    candidates = []

    # Structural lattice lines are almost entirely one color, apart from
    # occasional marker pixels at crossings.
    for color in colors:
        row_ids = [r for r in range(h)
                   if sum(v == color for v in grid[r]) >= 0.8 * w]
        col_ids = [c for c in range(w)
                   if sum(grid[r][c] == color for r in range(h)) >= 0.8 * h]
        rg, cg = _groups(row_ids), _groups(col_ids)
        if len(rg) < 2 or len(cg) < 2:
            continue
        # Favor thin, regular bands over a dominant fill color.
        row_gaps = [b[0] - a[0] for a, b in zip(rg, rg[1:])]
        col_gaps = [b[0] - a[0] for a, b in zip(cg, cg[1:])]
        regularity = len(set(row_gaps)) + len(set(col_gaps))
        thickness = sum(map(len, rg)) / len(rg) + sum(map(len, cg)) / len(cg)
        candidates.append((thickness + 0.01 * regularity, color, rg, cg))

    if not candidates:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    _, line, row_groups, col_groups = min(candidates, key=lambda x: x[0])
    rows = [g[len(g) // 2] for g in row_groups]
    cols = [g[len(g) // 2] for g in col_groups]

    row_band = {r for group in row_groups for r in group}
    col_band = {c for group in col_groups for c in group}
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_band and c not in col_band]
    blank = Counter(interior).most_common(1)[0][0] if interior else line

    # A reduced pixel is present only when all four surrounding lattice
    # crossings carry the same non-structural color. Other cells are blank.
    cells, marked = [], []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            value = corners[0]
            is_marked = value != line and all(v == value for v in corners)
            out_row.append(value if is_marked else blank)
            if is_marked:
                marked.append((i, j))
        cells.append(out_row)

    if not marked:
        return []
    r0 = min(r for r, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(r for r, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(c for _, c in marked)
    c1 = max(c for _, c in marked)
    return [row[c0:c1 + 1] for row in cells[r0:r1 + 1]]
